newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says sustainability is key EMU issue.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says sustainability is key EMU issue.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that the decisive issue for the Bundesbank is determining EMU fiscal criteria is sustainability.
"We consider all the criteria important," Tietmeyer said. "Inflation, interest rates, exchange rates and the condition of public finances."
"What is important is that the situation should be sustainable," he said.
Tietmeyer was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
He said the past, present and future developments would all play a part in the bank's decision.
"In our assessment of the public finances we have to look at the development in recent years, look at the current situation, and then look at the future," Tietmeyer said.
He added that although the reference levels laid down in the Maastricht Treaty were important, they were not the only basis for a decision.
"The three percent deficit target plays an important role in our assessment, as does the 60 percent (national debt target). But they are not the only factors in our decision," he said.
